- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; reduce subsequent forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If true price deviates from 30-day moving average by >2%, model often fails to mean-revert; adjust forecast toward recent average with decay factor (e.g., 0.85).
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment history shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive positive values), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch trend.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 2–3 periods.
- When true price drops below 65% of recent 7-day high, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to avoid “bottoming too early.”
